reader.requirement: At COBOL-85, for each file-name-3 of a SORT GIVING phrase, the compiler must refuse a sort file whose records are larger than the largest record described for file-name-3, and, when file-name-3 has variable length records (Format 2, or Format 3 which this implementation documents as variable, §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR13), also one whose records are smaller than its smallest described record; for Format 3 the record sizes are those of the record descriptions (§1985:VII.3.8.4 GR14), not integer-4/integer-5.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.RecordContainsRangeBindsRecordSize (active from 2002) sets VaryingRecordInfo.BoundsEnforced; false for a Format 3 clause at --std 85, so FileModel.RecordSizeRange sizes the file from its record descriptions (each at its maximum) instead of the stated integer-4/integer-5

reader.edition-search: Grep of SortBinder.cs, FileModel.RecordSizeRange/VaryMin/VaryMax and BindRecordClause for Edition/DialectLevel/DialectBehavior; ScreenTransferRecordSizes itself takes no edition (ctx.Edition only as the Reported sink).
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: for a Format 3 GIVING file (RECORD CONTAINS 5 TO 30 over records of 10 and 20) --std 85 bounds the sort records by the descriptions 10..20 and refuses 25- and 8-byte SD records; --std 2002/2023 bound them by the stated 5..30 and accept both
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb995_sort_merge_record_size_ranges runs only the legal edges with Format 1/Format 2 sequential files; it does not exercise the refusal half at 85, a Format 3 GIVING file, an ODO sort record, several GIVING files, or relative/indexed GIVING files

probes.printed: 9 x COBOL1757: Format 2 10..20 vs SD 25 and SD 5; fixed 20 vs SD 25; Format 3 10..20 vs SD 25 and SD 5; fixed 20 vs ODO SD (no RECORD clause, max 30); second GIVING file GV2 18..30 vs SD 15; indexed GI 20 vs SD 25; relative GR 20 vs SD 25
probes.expected: each refused under SR10 (larger than largest; smaller than smallest for a variable file)

probes.printed: SD 15 GIVING fixed 20, Format 3 10..20 and indexed 20: each file holds AAAAA/BBBBB/CCCCC a-/b-/c-data; ODO SD (7..20) GIVING Format 2 7..20: MMMMM01Q.., ZZZZZ03XYZ, length 20
--std 85: 2 x COBOL1757 (G35 describes variable-length records of 10 to 20 bytes vs SD 25 and SD 8); --std 2002 and 2023: EXIT 0
probes.expected: 85: records described for G35 are 10 and 20 (GR14 second sentence), so 25 and 8 are refused

reader.notes: One screen serves SORT/MERGE USING/GIVING; GIVING makes file-name-3 the bound. Format 3 is documented variable-length (docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-148.md). A file with an ODO record and no RECORD clause is treated as fixed at its maximum size (D-FRA implied Format 1), which 1985 leaves to the record description (§1985:VII.3.8.4 GR1); diagnostics cite the 2023 rule number SR11.
reader.at-2023: s10bad: the same 9 refusals; s10f3: accepted (stated bounds)

refuter.evidence: Read SR10 with §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR4 (Format 2 integers bound every record of the file), GR14 (Format 3 sizes defined by the record descriptions), §1985:XI.4.4.4 GR12b and §1985:II.2.1.4.3; SortBinder.cs#ScreenTransferRecordSizes over FileModel.cs#RecordSizeRange (BoundsEnforced false only for a Format 3 clause at --std 85, documented in docs/conformance DOC-A.1-148). Probes at --std 85: s10r1.cob compile: exactly 2 refusals of 8 SORTs: SD with no RECORD clause and records 10/25 GIVING fixed 20 (COBOL1757, SD fixed 25 under D-FRA) and SD VARYING 5..20 GIVING VARYING 10..20 (smaller than smallest); accepted: SD 25 and SD 8 GIVING VARYING FROM 5 TO 30 over records 10/20 (stated bounds, GR4), SD 25 GIVING explicit RECORD CONTAINS 30 over a 20-byte record (Format 1, GR3), SD 5 GIVING no-RECORD-clause file of records 10/20 (implied fixed 20, implementor-defined per II.2.1.4.3), SD VARYING 5..20 GIVING fixed 20 (upper bound only), Format 3 SD 5 TO 30 over records 10/20 GIVING fixed 20 (descriptions max 20). s10r3.cob run: 25-byte SD records GIVING VARYING 5 TO 30 DEPENDING ON WL over a 30-byte record: read back WL=25 [AAAAAabcdefghijklmnopqrst] then WL=25 [BBBBB...] = GR12b's size-as-sorted. s10r2.cob: LINE SEQUENTIAL refused at 85 (COBOL0900). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XI.4.4.3 SR10 ... the text is in SR10'; 'OK  §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR4 ... the text is in GR4'; 'OK  §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR14 ... the text is in GR14'; 'OK  §1985:XI.4.4.4 GR12b ... the text is in GR12b'. Reading stated: 'largest record described for file-name-3' is the stated integer-3 for Format 2 (GR4) and the descriptions for Format 3 at 85 (GR14 'However ... completely defined in the record description entry'); both arms consistent with the edition's text.
